newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes steady, Brent paper mixed.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes steady, Brent paper mixed.

text.p: North Sea crudes were broadly unchanged in quiet early Friday talk but Brent paper values were mixed, traders said.
July Brent paper shed three cents to $19.46 a barrel and intermonth spreads were also weaker, losing some of the support drawn partly from expectations of sharply lower North Sea loadings next month.
Brent June/July traded at evens after changing hands twice on Thursday at +5 cents. July/Aug also slipped to talk at -3/evens from +2 cents.
However, Brent CFDs were looking firmer, dealers said.
Next week's dates gained three cents to trade at July Brent -23 cents. There was also unconfirmed talk of the following week (May 27-30) trading at July Brent -21 cents.
Traders said Dated Brent should draw support from a wide open arbitrage to the United States, reflected in a robust July WTI/Brent spread which stood at around $1.80 early on Friday.
Four or five traders and refiners were heard offering Brent into the U.S. Gulf late on Thursday and there was unconfirmed talk of a June 22-27 arrival cargo fetching July WTI -80 cents.
The first two cargoes from the June Brent loading programme were due to turn wet on Friday, traders said.
The Forties programme, released early on Friday, showed June liftings would total 17.3 million barrels, equivalent to about 10 standard 500,000-barrel cargoes fewer than in May.
But some traders had been expecting a bigger impact from scheduled maintenance shutdowns.
"There has been a lot of focus on Forties in June with some people believing it would be much lower. I wouldn't say this news is bearish but it's probably neutral," said one.
Total North Sea loadings in June from the eight main export systems will fall by 260,000 bpd to 4.35 million bpd from 4.61 million in May. --Mark Thompson, London +44 171 542 7930
